stem: What are the coordinates of the vertex of the graph?
stimulus: A labour economist graphs $y = f(x)$, where $y$ is the number of parts a factory worker assembles per hour and $x$ is the number of hours since the start of a shift. In the graph, vertical gridlines are 1 unit apart and horizontal gridlines are 5 units apart. The graph is a parabola that opens downward. It crosses the $y$-axis at the 4th horizontal gridline above the origin. Its highest point lies on the vertical gridline $x = 4$, at the 8th horizontal gridline above the $x$-axis.
explanation: The vertex is the highest point of this parabola. It sits at $x = 4$. It is 8 gridlines up, and each horizontal gridline is 5 units, so $y = 8 \times 5 = 40$. The vertex is $(4, 40)$.

B.why: You swapped the coordinates. The x-coordinate comes first, so the vertex is $(4, 40)$, not $(40, 4)$.

C.why: You counted 8 gridlines but forgot that the vertical axis goes up in 5s. Eight gridlines stand for 40, not 8.

D.why: That is the y-intercept, where the graph crosses the $y$-axis. The question asks for the vertex, the turning point at the top of the curve.

stem: What is the y-intercept of the graph?
stimulus: A folklore scholar graphs $y = f(x)$, where $y$ is the number of recorded retellings of a regional legend in a decade and $x$ is the number of decades after 1900. In the graph, vertical gridlines are 1 unit apart and horizontal gridlines are 10 units apart. The graph is a parabola that opens upward. It crosses the $y$-axis at the 3rd horizontal gridline above the origin. Its lowest point is at $(4, 10)$.
explanation: The y-intercept is the point on the graph where $x = 0$. The curve crosses the $y$-axis 3 gridlines up, and each gridline is 10 units, so the y-intercept is $(0, 30)$.

A.why: You counted 3 gridlines as 3 units. The vertical axis goes up in 10s, so 3 gridlines stand for 30.

B.why: That is the vertex, the lowest point of the curve. The y-intercept is where the curve crosses the $y$-axis, at $x = 0$.

D.why: You swapped the coordinates. A y-intercept always has an x-coordinate of 0, so it is written $(0, 30)$.

stem: What is the y-intercept of the graph?
stimulus: A musicologist measures how quickly the vibration of a plucked harp string dies away. She graphs $y = f(x)$, where $y$ is the amplitude of the vibration, in millimeters, and $x$ is the time, in seconds, after the string is plucked. In the graph, vertical gridlines are 1 unit apart and horizontal gridlines are 2 units apart. The graph is a decreasing exponential curve. It crosses the $y$-axis at the 6th horizontal gridline above the origin, and it passes through the point $(2, 6)$.
explanation: The y-intercept is where $x = 0$. The curve crosses the $y$-axis 6 gridlines up, and each gridline is 2 units, so $y = 6 \times 2 = 12$. The y-intercept is $(0, 12)$.

A.why: You counted 6 gridlines as 6 units. The vertical axis goes up in 2s, so the 6th gridline stands for 12.

C.why: You swapped the coordinates. A y-intercept always has an x-coordinate of 0.

D.why: That is another point on the curve, 2 seconds after the pluck. The y-intercept is the point at $x = 0$.

stem: According to the graph, what is the maximum height, in meters, of the debris?
stimulus: To create a controlled seismic signal, a seismologist sets off a small blast on a quarry ledge. The graph shows $y = h(t)$, the height of a piece of debris above the quarry floor, in meters, $t$ seconds after the blast. In the graph, vertical gridlines are 1 second apart and horizontal gridlines are 10 meters apart. The graph is a parabola that opens downward. It crosses the vertical axis at the 2nd horizontal gridline. Its highest point lies on the vertical gridline $t = 3$, at the 5th horizontal gridline.
explanation: The maximum height is the y-coordinate of the vertex. The highest point is 5 gridlines up, and each gridline is 10 meters, so the maximum height is $5 \times 10 = 50$ meters.

A.why: 3 is the x-coordinate of the vertex. It is the time when the debris is highest, not the height it reaches.

B.why: You counted 5 gridlines but forgot that the vertical axis goes up in 10s. Five gridlines stand for 50 meters.

C.why: 20 meters is the height at $t = 0$, the y-intercept. That is the starting height on the ledge, not the maximum.

stem: What are the coordinates of the minimum point of the graph?
stimulus: A textile historian graphs $y = p(x)$, the market price, in shillings, of a bolt of printed calico $x$ years after 1800. In the graph, vertical gridlines are 5 units apart and horizontal gridlines are 2 units apart. The graph is a parabola that opens upward. It crosses the $y$-axis at the 8th horizontal gridline. Its lowest point lies on the 3rd vertical gridline to the right of the origin, at the 4th horizontal gridline.
explanation: The minimum point is the lowest point of the parabola. It is 3 gridlines right at 5 units each, so $x = 15$. It is 4 gridlines up at 2 units each, so $y = 8$. The minimum point is $(15, 8)$.

A.why: You swapped the coordinates. The horizontal value, 15, comes first.

C.why: You counted gridlines without using the scales. The horizontal axis goes up in 5s and the vertical axis goes up in 2s.

D.why: That is the y-intercept, where the curve crosses the $y$-axis. The question asks for the lowest point.

stem: What is the y-coordinate of the y-intercept of the graph?
stimulus: An agricultural scientist graphs $y = f(x)$, the yield of a wheat plot, in bushels, when $x$ kilograms of nitrogen fertilizer are applied. In the graph, vertical gridlines are 10 units apart and horizontal gridlines are 5 units apart. The graph is a parabola that opens downward. It crosses the $y$-axis at the 6th horizontal gridline above the origin. Its highest point is at $(40, 70)$.
explanation: The y-intercept is where $x = 0$, which here means no fertilizer. The curve crosses the $y$-axis 6 gridlines up, and each gridline is 5 units, so the y-coordinate is $6 \times 5 = 30$.

B.why: You counted 6 gridlines as 6 units. The vertical axis goes up in 5s, so the 6th gridline stands for 30.

C.why: 70 is the maximum yield, the y-coordinate of the vertex. The question asks where the curve crosses the $y$-axis.

D.why: 40 is the x-coordinate of the vertex, the amount of fertilizer that gives the highest yield. It is not the y-intercept.

stem: What are the coordinates of the vertex of the graph?
stimulus: An archaeologist draws the cross-section of an ancient drainage ditch. The graph shows $y = d(x)$, the elevation of the ditch floor, in meters, relative to the surrounding ground, at a horizontal distance of $x$ meters from one edge. In the graph, vertical gridlines are 2 units apart and horizontal gridlines are 1 unit apart. The graph is a parabola that opens upward. It crosses the $x$-axis at $x = 0$ and at $x = 8$. Its lowest point lies on the 2nd vertical gridline to the right of the origin, 3 horizontal gridlines below the $x$-axis.
explanation: The vertex is the lowest point of the ditch. It is 2 gridlines right, and each gridline is 2 units, so $x = 4$. It is 3 gridlines below the axis at 1 unit each, so $y = -3$. The vertex is $(4, -3)$. It sits halfway between the x-intercepts 0 and 8, which confirms it.

A.why: You counted 2 gridlines as 2 units. The horizontal axis goes up in 2s, so the 2nd gridline is at $x = 4$.

B.why: You swapped the coordinates. The horizontal value, 4, comes first.

C.why: That is an x-intercept, where the ditch meets ground level. The vertex is the lowest point of the curve.

stem: What is the y-coordinate of the y-intercept of the graph?
stimulus: An astronomer graphs $y = N(x)$, the number of near-Earth asteroids catalogued by a sky survey, $x$ years after the survey began. In the graph, vertical gridlines are 1 unit apart and horizontal gridlines are 25 units apart. The graph is an increasing exponential curve. It crosses the $y$-axis at the 2nd horizontal gridline above the origin, and it passes through the points $(1, 100)$ and $(2, 200)$.
explanation: The y-intercept is where $x = 0$, the start of the survey. The curve crosses the $y$-axis 2 gridlines up, and each gridline is 25 units, so the y-coordinate is $2 \times 25 = 50$.

A.why: You assumed the curve starts at the origin. This exponential curve crosses the $y$-axis above zero, at the 2nd gridline.

B.why: You counted 2 gridlines as 2 units. The vertical axis goes up in 25s, so the 2nd gridline stands for 50.

D.why: 100 is the count one year into the survey, at $x = 1$. The y-intercept is the value at $x = 0$.
